clue.text: Disorderly male with case in Jumbo? Never!

indicators.note: something disorderly is out of order, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A badly behaved man with a suitcase climbs inside an elephant, to cries of protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disorderly' rearranges M and CASEIN. The definition rests on the saying that an elephant (Jumbo) never forgets, so a forgetful elephant is unthinkable.
explanation.definitionFit: Elephants proverbially never forget, so a forgetting elephant, one suffering memory loss, is what the exclamation rejects.

clue.text: It takes a pound to secure rises, though

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising reads the word from the bottom up, so it is turned round

parts.note: to secure is to tie

explanation.surface: Even so, it takes money to fasten things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' turns TIE to EIT; 'It takes' merely links.
explanation.definitionFit: Albeit is a conjunction meaning even if or although.

clue.text: Choir involved with NW cathedral city

indicators.note: letters involved together are mixed up, giving a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A choir takes part with a north-western cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: Norwich in Norfolk has a Norman cathedral and city status.

clue.text: Fast-moving English river within catchment area

indicators.note: one piece sits within the other, inside it
moving letters are shifted about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the Tyne is a river in north-east England

explanation.surface: A swift English river runs through the land that drains into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges the first piece and E, and 'within' puts the river inside. The hydrological 'catchment area' is used wittily for a net that catches falling performers.
explanation.definitionFit: A net strung below acrobats catches anyone who falls, so it is literally a place for catching.

clue.text: Small boat makes sea creatures dive

parts.note: cockles are edible shellfish
a dive is a squalid, disreputable place, a hell or hellhole

explanation.surface: A dinghy causes the shellfish to plunge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dive' looks like a verb but is the noun for a seedy bar or den.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockleshell is a small, light boat, frail as a shell.

clue.text: Go back to find right exit

parts.note: an egress is a way out

explanation.surface: Retreat to look for the correct way out.
explanation.definitionFit: To regress is to revert or return to an earlier state.

clue.text: Rose after 10

definitions.meaning: the traffic light that follows the one at 10 across

explanation.walkthrough: 10 across is AMBER: on British traffic lights the steady amber is followed by red.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep pink colour, and the stop signal that follows the amber light.

clue.text: White of egg has a hard look, they say

indicators.note: what people say is heard, so the letters are spelt by sound

parts.note: a glare is a fierce stare

explanation.surface: The egg white seems to stare fiercely, people claim.
explanation.definitionFit: Glair is egg white used as a glaze or size, especially in bookbinding.

clue.text: Hold me up, provide support

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
to brace is to support or strengthen

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be lifted and propped up.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace someone is to hold them in one's arms.

clue.text: Vagrant gets near Troy, perhaps

indicators.note: a vagrant wanders about, so the letters wander into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tramp approaches the ancient city of Troy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Troy' suggests the ancient city; it is Sergeant Frank Troy, the soldier in Hardy's Far from the Madding Crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Troy in Hardy's novel holds the army rank above corporal, so he is one example.

clue.text: Showing cheek, being clean-shaven

definitions.meaning: literally with a bare face, no beard

explanation.definitionFit: Barefaced means openly impudent, and literally describes a face with no beard.

clue.text: A sort of honour king gives Winsor's heroine

parts.note: the MBE (Member of the Order of the British Empire) is a British honour
R (Rex) is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch hands a decoration to a novelist's leading lady.
explanation.walkthrough: Kathleen Winsor wrote the 1944 novel Forever Amber, whose heroine is Amber St Clare.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Kathleen Winsor's novel Forever Amber is a woman named Amber St Clare.

clue.text: I'll be found in one spot — that's natural

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: the letter will be found in, meaning it is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: a spot is a dot
I'll means I will, so the letter I itself is what goes in

explanation.surface: A person announces where they will be found, adding that this is quite normal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Natural' is an old noun for a simpleton or person of low intelligence, not the adjective it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: In old usage a natural was a person born simple-minded, a fool.

clue.text: Minor characters unheard in High Court?

definitions.meaning: small letters as opposed to capitals
a lesser legal matter, one heard in an inferior court rather than the High Court

explanation.definitionFit: Small letters are printed from the lower compartment of a printer's type case, and a lesser legal action is jokingly a lower case.

clue.text: I'll accept that fine after spring, too

indicators.note: one piece comes after another, following it

parts.note: a well is a spring of water
and means too, in addition
good means fine

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to pay a fine after the spring season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine' looks like a penalty but means good.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase of grudging assent, meaning that is acceptable so far.

clue.text: Plant producing lighting for Shanghai, say

definitions.meaning: a physalis, with papery orange calyces
a paper lamp of the kind used in a city in China

explanation.definitionFit: Physalis alkekengi is called by this name, and the paper lamp from China shares it.

clue.text: Evening paper taken up by almost everyone

parts.note: nigh means nearly, almost

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means read from the bottom up, reversing

parts.note: FT, the Financial Times, is a newspaper
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Nearly everyone picks up the evening newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' looks as if it trims 'everyone'; it is NIGH, and 'taken up' turns FT to TF.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightfall is dusk, the start of the evening.

clue.text: Put on spur, but not the second

indicators.note: the second letter of the word is left out

parts.note: to spur is to stimulate

explanation.surface: A rider attaches a spur, leaving the other one off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on' means feign, not dress in.
explanation.definitionFit: To put on a manner is to feign or fake it.

clue.text: It began to rain hard, being blustery as well

indicators.note: blustery weather blows things about, so the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
H is the standard abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A weather report: rain set in heavily and the wind got up too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being blustery' shuffles ITBEGANTORAIN and H, from 'hard', into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase meaning additionally or besides, as an extra thrown in on a deal.

clue.text: Soldiers trapped by river in flood

indicators.note: something trapped by another is enclosed inside it

parts.note: the Trent is a major river in the English Midlands
OR, other ranks, is the crossword abbreviation for soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops are cut off by a river that has burst its banks.
explanation.definitionFit: A torrent is a violent rushing flow of water.

clue.text: I call round towards evening

indicators.note: one piece goes round another, enclosing it

parts.note: to ring is to call on the phone
on means towards, as in marching on the city

explanation.surface: I telephone around dusk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evening' is not dusk but making even, smoothing out clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing creases out of fabric smooths it, making it even.

clue.text: This was instrumental in splitting leaders of Spanish and French

indicators.note: one piece splits another apart, sitting inside it

parts.note: the leading two letters of the word Spanish
et is French for and
taken as written

explanation.surface: A thing that played a part in dividing the heads of Spain and France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instrumental' means it was a musical instrument, not that it helped.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinet is a small harpsichord, a keyboard musical instrument of old.

clue.text: Composed without any frills?

definitions.meaning: literally not ruffled, having no ruffs or frills

explanation.definitionFit: Someone calm is not ruffled, and a plain garment literally lacks ruffles.

clue.text: Tree sheltering a king, a devout man

indicators.note: the tree shelters, enclosing the other letters

parts.note: a fir is a conifer
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch takes cover under a tree, as does a holy man.
explanation.definitionFit: A fakir is a Muslim or Hindu ascetic holy man living on alms.

clue.text: Soldiers put back in first cavalry unit

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other, placed inside it

parts.note: top means first, as in top of the class

indicators.note: putting something back turns it round, so these letters read in reverse

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is the usual crossword abbreviation for soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops are returned to the leading mounted regiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldiers' looks like the definition, but 'cavalry unit' is; 'put back' turns the soldiers round and 'in' places them inside the word for first.
explanation.definitionFit: A troop is the subunit of a cavalry squadron, the horse soldiers' equivalent of an infantry platoon.

clue.text: Copy a king, being upright

parts.note: to ape is to copy
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Mimicking a monarch while standing straight.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a nautical word: an anchor or oar is apeak when held vertical.
explanation.definitionFit: In sailing usage an anchor cable or oar held vertically is said to be in this position.

clue.text: Professional cricketer, one on trial

parts.note: a pro is a professional
a bat is a batsman in cricket
the Roman numeral for one is I
taken as written

explanation.surface: A paid cricket player is being given a tryout.
explanation.definitionFit: A probation is a trial period testing someone's suitability or conduct.

clue.text: China cup, a Limoges piece

indicators.note: a piece of the words is taken, the letters running across them

explanation.surface: A porcelain cup, an item of French china.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is rhyming slang: china plate = mate, a friend; not porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: In cockney rhyming slang china plate means mate, a friend.

clue.text: 10% taking oral, with leaders out to get entrance

indicators.note: the first letters of the two pieces are dropped, as leaders leave

parts.note: ten percent is a tenth
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tenth of the marks goes to the spoken exam, and the top people leave to gain admission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' is the verb (en-TRANCE), to bewitch, not a doorway. 'with leaders out' removes the T of TENTH and the O of ORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To enthral is to captivate or hold spellbound.

clue.text: Entrance of French star, for instance

parts.note: de is French for of
a star is an example of a light in the sky

explanation.surface: A Gallic celebrity makes her entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: Again 'Entrance' is the verb, to charm, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To delight someone is to charm or enchant them.
